request.contents:
Does the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 (Ontario) make this clause of a residential tenancy agreement void?

Read the clause as a term of an ordinary private residential tenancy in Ontario that the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 covers: the rental unit has no exemption under section 6.1, and it is not student housing, a care home, a co-operative or a mobile home park.

Decide using only the sections of the Act below. They are a selection, not the whole Act.

<sections>
[The headings and text of sections 4, 14, 15, 20, 22, 25, 26, 27, 34, 37, 40, 105, 106, 108, 116, 119, 120, 134 of the Act, from e-Laws; SHA-256 170f924284b858615f0e872622e0e1150d171bcaeffe1a8e61a2ea40a42b0e8c. Left out of saved records.]
</sections>

<clause>
Once the Landlord and the Tenant have agreed that the tenancy will end, the Landlord may show the unit to prospective tenants between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. without written notice, after informing the Tenant, or making a reasonable effort to inform the Tenant, before each visit.
</clause>

Answer with:
- verdict: "void" if the Act makes the clause void, "allowed" if the Act permits it, or "unsure" if these sections don't let you decide.
- section: the number of the one section that decides it, such as "14", without a subsection. Empty if unsure.
- quote: the words of that section that decide it, copied exactly: one continuous passage from a single subsection, at least five words, with nothing left out, added or changed. Not a heading. Empty if unsure.
- reason: one or two sentences.

text: {"verdict":"allowed","section":"26","quote":"A landlord may enter the rental unit without written notice to show the unit to prospective tenants","reason":"Section 26(3) expressly permits a landlord to enter a rental unit without written notice between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. to show it to prospective tenants once the landlord and tenant have agreed to terminate the tenancy, provided the landlord informs or makes a reasonable effort to inform the tenant before entering. Because the clause mirrors all the statutory conditions in section 26(3), it is consistent with the Act and allowed."}

parsed.quote: A landlord may enter the rental unit without written notice to show the unit to prospective tenants
parsed.reason: Section 26(3) expressly permits a landlord to enter a rental unit without written notice between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. to show it to prospective tenants once the landlord and tenant have agreed to terminate the tenancy, provided the landlord informs or makes a reasonable effort to inform the tenant before entering. Because the clause mirrors all the statutory conditions in section 26(3), it is consistent with the Act and allowed.
